# Dvattiṁsākāra (Kp 3 (PTS Kp 2))

**ID:** Kp 3 (PTS Kp 2)
**Section:** Khuddakapāṭha (kp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Dvattiṁsākāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0501m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dvattiṁsākāra* ("The Thirty-two Parts of the Body", translated by Mrs. Rhys Davids as "the thirty-two fold formation") is the third text of the *Khuddakapāṭha* [Hazra 1994; Williams and Ladwig 2012]. It consists of a bare enumeration of thirty-six Pali words listing thirty-two parts or impurities of the human body, such as the hair of the head, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, spleen, lungs, intestines, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, and mucus [Dhammika, Broken Buddha; Hazra 1994]. The text serves as a meditative reflection designed to engender detachment and revulsion toward the physical body [Dhammika, Broken Buddha; Kalupahana 2001]. Notably, the text includes the brain in the skull (*matthake matthaluṅgaṁ*), a constituent not found in the standard thirty-one-part contemplation list of the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta* of the *Dīgha Nikāya* or the *Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta* of the *Majjhima Nikāya* [Hazra 1994]. Alongside its place in the canonical *Khuddakapāṭha*, the text is included in the opening portion of the traditional Theravāda paritta collection known as the *Catubhāṇavārapāḷi* [Anālayo 2018; Holz, Bhadrakarātrī-sūtra; Kalupahana 2001].

Rhys Davids [Hazra 1994].
